statements.statement: The paper has been withdrawn at the request of the editor, and the full text and PDF have been replaced by the withdrawal statement.
The editor was told that the indoor temperature records had been processed with an incorrect sensor calibration, and the reported results cannot be relied on.
The paper's headline results, including 2.1 °C lower mean daily peak indoor temperature, came from indoor temperature data, and another was 41% fewer hours above 28 °C in living rooms.
Draft sets the green roof indoor cooling effect to 2.1 °C, described as the reduction measured by Okafor et al. [14], parameter described in Section 2.2.
The paper reported a mean daily peak indoor temperature 2.1 °C lower in green-roofed flats than in paired control flats.
Draft says its estimate rests above all on the indoor cooling effect, scales with the 2.1 °C, and halving would mean green roofs no longer outperform reflective coatings.
The paper has been withdrawn at the editor's request: records processed with incorrect sensor calibration, so results cannot be relied on.
The paper's full text and PDF have been replaced by the withdrawal statement.
The paper has been withdrawn at the editor's request and the records had incorrect sensor calibration, so results cannot be relied on.
Draft sets the cooling effect to 2.1 °C, described as measured by Okafor et al. [14], while the paper reported 2.1 °C lower mean daily peak than paired controls.
Draft says the result scales with the 2.1 °C and that halving it would mean green roofs no longer outperform reflective coatings.
